lessons.title: What Are Question Tags?
lessons.content: A question tag is a short question added to the end of a statement. It is used to confirm information or ask for agreement. Question tags always use pronouns, and the auxiliary verb must match the tense of the main verb.

details.explanation: A question tag turns a statement into a question. It is separated by a comma from the main statement.
details.example: You are a student, aren't you?
details.burmese: မင်း ကျောင်းသားတစ်ယောက်ပါ၊ မဟုတ်ဘူးလား?

details.explanation: Question tags are used to check information or ask for confirmation from the listener.
details.example: It's cold today, isn't it?
details.burmese: ဒီနေ့ အအေးချမ်းတယ်၊ မချမ်းဘူးလား?

details.explanation: Statement + comma + auxiliary verb + pronoun + question mark
details.example: She likes coffee, doesn't she?

details.explanation: Always use pronouns in question tags, even if the statement uses a proper noun.
details.example: Jack is from Spain, isn't he?
details.burmese: Jack က စပိန်က လာတယ်၊ မလာဘူးလား?

lessons.title: Positive Statements, Negative Tags
lessons.content: When the statement is positive, the question tag is negative. This is the most common pattern for question tags.

details.rule: Positive statement with is/are → negative tag with isn't/aren't
details.example: Jack is from Spain, isn't he?
details.burmese: Jack က စပိန်က လာတယ်၊ မလာဘူးလား?

details.rule: Positive statement with V1/V1+s → negative tag with don't/doesn't
details.example: You play the guitar, don't you?
details.burmese: မင်း ဂစ်တာ တီးတယ်၊ မတီးဘူးလား?

details.rule: Positive statement with was/were → negative tag with wasn't/weren't
details.example: The film was fantastic, wasn't it?
details.burmese: ရုပ်ရှင်က အရမ်းကောင်းတယ်၊ မကောင်းဘူးလား?

details.rule: Positive statement with V2 → negative tag with didn't
details.example: You went there, didn't you?

details.rule: Positive statement with will → negative tag with won't
details.example: You will pass the exam, won't you?
details.burmese: မင်း စာမေးပွဲ အောင်မယ်၊ အောင်မှာမဟုတ်ဘူးလား?

details.rule: Positive statement with have/has + V3 → negative tag with haven't/hasn't
details.example: You have studied all week, haven't you?
details.burmese: မင်း တစ်ပတ်လုံး စာလေ့လာခဲ့တယ်၊ မလေ့လာခဲ့ဘူးလား?

details.rule: Positive statement with can/must/should/would → negative tag with can't/mustn't/shouldn't/wouldn't
details.example: Mary can speak English, can't she?
details.burmese: Mary က အင်္ဂလိပ် ပြောတတ်တယ်၊ မပြောတတ်ဘူးလား?

lessons.title: Negative Statements, Positive Tags
lessons.content: When the statement is negative, the question tag is positive. This reverses the pattern used for positive statements.

details.rule: Negative statement with isn't/aren't → positive tag with is/are
details.example: He isn't crazy, is he?

details.rule: Negative statement with don't/doesn't → positive tag with do/does
details.example: You don't go there, do you?

details.rule: Negative statement with wasn't/weren't → positive tag with was/were
details.example: He wasn't sick, was he?
details.burmese: သူ မနာဘူး၊ နာလား?

details.rule: Negative statement with didn't → positive tag with did
details.example: You didn't do your homework, did you?
details.burmese: မင်း အိမ်စာ မလုပ်ခဲ့ဘူး၊ လုပ်ခဲ့လား?

details.rule: Negative statement with won't → positive tag with will
details.example: You won't fail the exam, will you?

details.rule: Negative statement with haven't/hasn't + V3 → positive tag with have/has
details.example: You haven't been here all week, have you?
details.burmese: မင်း တစ်ပတ်လုံး ဒီမှာ မရှိခဲ့ဘူး၊ ရှိခဲ့လား?

details.rule: Negative statement with can't/mustn't/shouldn't/wouldn't → positive tag with can/must/should/would
details.example: John can't drive a car, can he?
details.burmese: John က ကား မမောင်းတတ်ဘူး၊ မောင်းတတ်လား?

lessons.title: Question Tags with Different Tenses
lessons.content: The auxiliary verb in the question tag must match the tense of the main verb in the statement. Each tense has its own auxiliary verb pattern.

details.example_negative: She doesn't work in a hotel, does she?
details.burmese: Sue က တင်းနစ် ကြိုက်တယ်၊ မကြိုက်ဘူးလား?

details.example_positive: John knew about this letter, didn't he?
details.example_negative: You didn't do your homework, did you?
details.burmese: John က ဒီစာအကြောင်း သိတယ်၊ မသိဘူးလား?

details.example_positive: You will pass the exam, won't you?
details.example_negative: You won't fail the exam, will you?
details.burmese: မင်း စာမေးပွဲ အောင်မယ်၊ အောင်မှာမဟုတ်ဘူးလား?

details.example_positive: You have studied all week, haven't you?
details.example_negative: She hasn't written a letter, has she?
details.burmese: မင်း တစ်ပတ်လုံး စာလေ့လာခဲ့တယ်၊ မလေ့လာခဲ့ဘူးလား?

details.example_positive: You had arrived before he left, hadn't you?
details.example_negative: You hadn't done it before, had you?
details.burmese: သူ မထွက်ခင် မင်း ရောက်ပြီးပြီ၊ မရောက်ခင်ဘူးလား?

details.example_positive: Mary can speak English, can't she?
details.example_negative: John can't drive a car, can he?
details.burmese: Mary က အင်္ဂလိပ် ပြောတတ်တယ်၊ မပြောတတ်ဘူးလား?

details.example_positive: We must be patient, mustn't we?
details.example_negative: We mustn't say anything, must we?
details.burmese: ငါတို့ စိတ်ရှည်ရပါမယ်၊ မရှည်ရဘူးလား?

details.example_positive: You should go now, shouldn't you?
details.example_negative: He shouldn't say things like that, should he?
details.burmese: မင်း အခု သွားသင့်တယ်၊ မသွားသင့်ဘူးလား?

lessons.title: Special Cases and Exceptions
lessons.content: Some statements require special question tag patterns that don't follow the standard positive→negative or negative→positive rules.

details.rule: Use 'aren't I?' instead of 'amn't I?'
details.example: I am attractive, aren't I?
details.burmese: ကျွန်မ ဆွဲဆောင်မှု ရှိတယ်၊ မရှိဘူးလား?

details.rule: Use 'am I?' for negative 'I am not' statements
details.example: I am not the person with the tickets, am I?
details.burmese: ကျွန်မ လက်မှတ်ပိုင်ရှင် မဟုတ်ဘူး၊ ဟုတ်လား?

details.rule: Use 'will you?' after imperative statements
details.example: Close the window, will you?
details.burmese: ပြတင်းပေါက် ပိတ်ပါ၊ ပိတ်မလား?

details.rule: Use 'shall we?' after 'Let's' statements
details.example: Let's go to the beach, shall we?

details.rule: Use a positive tag with 'they' or 'it'
details.example: Nobody lives in this house, do they?
details.burmese: ဘယ်သူမှ ဒီအိမ်မှာ မနေဘူး၊ နေကြလား?

details.rule: Use 'did it?' with 'nothing' statements
details.example: Nothing bad happened, did it?
details.burmese: ဘာမဆိုးတာ မဖြစ်ခဲ့ဘူး၊ ဖြစ်ခဲ့လား?

details.rule: Use 'do/does/did' instead of 'have/has/had'
details.example: You have a Ferrari, don't you?
details.burmese: မင်းမှာ Ferrari ရှိတယ်၊ မရှိဘူးလား?

details.rule: Use 'are there' or 'is there' depending on the statement
details.example: There aren't any spiders, are there?

details.rule: Use 'isn't it?' for 'This is...' statements
details.example: This is Paul's pen, isn't it?
details.burmese: ဒါ Paul ရဲ့ ဘောပင်ပါ၊ မဟုတ်ဘူးလား?
